userStories.title: Extend blocked-marker schema with dedup-key + consecutive-count logic
userStories.description: As the harness, I need a durable dedup key and a consecutive-blocked counter on the implement-blocked marker so that repeated identical deterministic blocks on the same story are detectable across sessions.
acceptanceCriteria: ImplementBlockedMarker (src/supervisor/implement-blocked-marker.ts) gains required consecutiveCount: number and keyHash: string plus optional escalated?: boolean and haltedAt?: string; readImplementBlockedMarker parses markers both with and without the new fields (backward compatible with CAM-195-era markers that lack them). [oracle: grep -q 'consecutiveCount' src/supervisor/implement-blocked-marker.ts]

A pure advanceBlockedMarker(prev, params, prdHash, threshold=3) computes a dedup key = sha256 over (storyId, the BLOCKED_* token, prdHash); when the new key matches prev.keyHash it increments consecutiveCount, when it differs it resets consecutiveCount to 1, rewrites keyHash, and clears escalated. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/implement-blocked-marker.test.ts]

At the threshold (3rd consecutive identical key) advanceBlockedMarker sets escalated:true and stamps haltedAt; counts 1 and 2 leave escalated falsy and haltedAt absent. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/implement-blocked-marker.test.ts]

The BLOCKED_* token is extracted from the marker reason string via /BLOCKED_\w+/ (the collapsed 'blocked' WorkerOutcomeKind is insufficient); a reason carrying no BLOCKED_ token falls back to a stable literal so the key stays deterministic. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/implement-blocked-marker.test.ts]

Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]

userStories.notes: Marker module: src/supervisor/implement-blocked-marker.ts; tests in test/supervisor/implement-blocked-marker.test.ts. Keep advanceBlockedMarker pure and clock-free (mirror the existing loop.ts/host.ts clock-free-seam split: haltedAt/writtenAt timestamps are stamped by the caller, not this pure fn). Reuse Bun.CryptoHasher('sha256') as in src/supervisor/suggestion-followups.ts rather than node:crypto. keyHash sources the token from the reason string, per gotcha: the specific BLOCKED_AMBIGUITY vs BLOCKED_QUALITY token only survives in outcome.detail/reason (result.ts:462 'Worker reported BLOCKED_... story=...'), never in the event-log WorkerOutcomeKind. Patterns: grep scripts/cam/patterns.md for 'Durable marker module template' (CAM-204) for the read-shape-guard/never-throws conventions this module already follows.

userStories.title: Wire the counter + PRD content-hash into the marker writer
userStories.description: As the harness, I need the production marker writer to feed the current PRD hash and prior marker through advanceBlockedMarker on every blocked terminal so that the persisted count reflects real cross-session repetition and resets on a genuine PRD amendment.
acceptanceCriteria: host.ts writeImplementBlockedMarkerFn reads the existing marker and the current sha256 of prd.json, calls advanceBlockedMarker, and persists the extended marker on every blocked terminal (still stamping writtenAt). [oracle: grep -q 'advanceBlockedMarker' src/supervisor/host.ts]

Repeated identical blocked terminals (same story, same BLOCKED_* token, unchanged prd.json) drive consecutiveCount monotonically 1 -> 2 -> 3; changing prd.json content (new sha256) on the next blocked terminal resets consecutiveCount to 1 and clears escalated (recovery on PRD amendment). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/implement-blocked-marker-wiring.test.ts]

sha256 is computed over prd.json file bytes at write time; an unreadable/absent prd.json degrades gracefully (marker still written, treated as a reset key) and never throws out of the writer. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/implement-blocked-marker-wiring.test.ts]

Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]

userStories.title: Halt the auto-dispatch chain when the marker is escalated
userStories.description: As the operator, I need the sidecar auto-chain to stop re-dispatching a story that has hit the circuit-breaker threshold so that ~10 wasted fresh implementer sessions against the same deterministic contradiction become at most 3.
acceptanceCriteria: After a 'blocked' terminal, runSidecarLoop reads the implement-blocked marker; when escalated:true it does NOT call flipActiveFn at the re-dispatch decision point (src/supervisor/loop.ts auto-chain, currently ~loop.ts:2157) and the loop stays active:false instead of re-spinning. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/sidecar-loop.test.ts]

When the marker is absent or escalated is falsy, the auto-chain proceeds exactly as before (flipActiveFn is called when hasPendingStories() is true). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/sidecar-loop.test.ts]

Default/ci-gated behavior is unchanged: with flipActiveFn absent (plan_approval !== 'auto') the breaker is inert and the loop pauses for a human cam next as today. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/sidecar-loop.test.ts]
On halt a structured event records the circuit-broken reason to the event log via the existing emitter, without inventing a new WorkerEventKind. [oracle: grep -q 'circuit' src/supervisor/loop.ts]

Recovery: after the marker is consumed on a DONE outcome (CAM-195 clearImplementBlockedMarkerForCurrentIssue) or reset by a PRD amendment (US-002), the auto-chain re-enables on the next blocked-or-progress cycle; the loop never stays halted across a real amendment. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/sidecar-loop.test.ts]

userStories.title: Surface the circuit-broken blocker in the orchestrator boot-read
userStories.description: As the operator, I need a distinct circuit-broken blocker line at orchestrator boot so that a halted auto-chain is visible and I know a PRD amendment (not a retry) is required.
acceptanceCriteria: The orchestrator boot-read (templates/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md) adds an escalated:true branch surfacing a distinct circuit-broken line, e.g. '⚠ implement circuit-broken: issue #<issueId> story <id> (<N> identical BLOCKED_...) — needs PRD amendment', keeping the existing non-escalated 'implement blocked' line for the escalated:false case.
